title: CriticalFL: A Critical Learning Periods Augmented Client Selection Framework for Efficient Federated Learning

problem.claim: Federated learning must improve efficiency while handling client heterogeneity and training phases that may differ in importance.

gap.claim: Adaptive client selection based on client training progress is not yet well-understood, and existing methods implicitly treat all learning phases as equally important.

contributions.claim: The paper develops CriticalFL, a critical learning period augmented federated learning framework that guides client selection using discovered critical learning periods.
CriticalFL augments existing federated learning methods with critical learning period information for adaptive client selection.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments using various machine learning models and datasets report consistently improved model accuracy and better communication efficiency compared with state-of-the-art methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Federated learning distributes data samples across multiple clients for distributed optimization.
Training-progress-aware adaptive client selection is increasingly used for efficiency but remains insufficiently understood.
Existing federated learning methods generally assume that all training phases are equally important.
Critical learning period findings challenge that assumption because small gradient errors during those periods may irreversibly reduce final test accuracy.
CriticalFL uses discovered critical learning periods to guide client selection, with reported experiments showing improved accuracy and communication efficiency.

source_observation.claim: Some learning phases may be disproportionately important because small gradient errors during critical learning periods can cause irrecoverable final accuracy deficiencies.

interpretation.claim: Training or resource allocation strategies may benefit from distinguishing phases by their effect on eventual model quality.

application.claim: Use phase-aware signals to guide client selection or other adaptive decisions in federated learning.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported models, datasets, or federated learning settings.

unknowns: How critical learning periods are discovered or measured.
Which client-selection mechanism and federated learning baselines are used.
The magnitude of reported accuracy and communication-efficiency improvements.
The experimental settings, datasets, models, and statistical evaluation details.
